title: Decode Ways
summary: Decode a digit string by splitting it into codes from 1 through 26.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–100 decimal digits. Leading zeros are allowed in the input. The result fits a signed 32-bit integer.

statement: Decode a digit string by splitting it into codes from 1 through 26. Each code represents one letter. Count valid splits. Codes cannot begin with 0.

examples.explanation: Neither 30 nor a standalone 0 is a code.

constraints: 1–100 decimal digits. Leading zeros are allowed in the input. The result fits a signed 32-bit integer.
hints: Conceptual: A zero can appear only as the second digit of an allowed two-digit code.
Directional: At each position, check the one-digit and two-digit choices separately.
Implementation: Count ways to finish each suffix. The empty suffix contributes one way. Cap oversized intermediate counts if using fixed-width arithmetic.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) extra space with rolling counts.
